review: 1:3–1:4 נִגְלֵיתָ בַּבָּשָׂר / בִּדְמוּת עֲבָדִים — 1 Timothy 3:16 (נִגְלָה בַבָּשָׂר) with Phil 2:7 (דְּמוּת עֲבָדִים); the Arabic ظَهَرْتَ بِالْجَسَد / فِي صُورَةِ الْعَبِيد is those two verses, and Hebrew keeps both nouns.

2:1–2:2 נֶעֱבָד מִן־ / הַמַּלְאָכִים וְהַצְּבָאוֹת — the Arabic وَأَنْتَ مَخْدُومٌ مِنَ الْـ / ـأَمْلَاكِ وَالْجُنُود splits the article of الْمَلَاك across the line break, which Hebrew cannot do; the sentence is re-cut whole at the boundary.

2:3 שֶׁשֵּׁרְתָּנוּ — 'that You served us'; the Arabic خَدَمْتَنَا is the same verb as the angels' service in the previous line, and Hebrew keeps the root עבד/שׁרת deliberately to sharpen the contrast.
5:4 צִדְּךָ הַמְּדֻקָּר — John 19:34 (צִדּוֹ … דָּקַר); the Arabic جَنْبَكَ الْمَطْعُون is 'Your pierced side', and דקר is the verb of the spear.
6:2 פְּצָעֶיךָ — 'Your wounds'; the Arabic جِرَاحَكَ is the wounds shown to Thomas (John 20:27), and פֶּצַע is the biblical word for a wound (Isa 1:6).
